title: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems with machine learning potentials
title_zh: 文献研究：Atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems with machine learning potentials
summary: Modern machine learning potentials (MLPs) enable large-scale atomistic simulations at unprecedented accuracy. The incorporation of explicit physical interactions such as long-range electrostatics has…
abstract: arXiv:2611.15939v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern machine learning potentials (MLPs) enable large-scale atomistic simulations at unprecedented accuracy. The incorporation of explicit physical interactions such as long-range electrostatics has continuously broadened their applicability to increasingly complex systems in chemistry and materials science. Extending MLPs to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis, however, is still challenging as it requires the consideration of electrode potentials and electric fields in the atomic interactions. Such approaches have emerged only recently, and although the field is evolving rapidly, further conceptual advances are still needed for carrying out reliable simulations at finite temperature under applied potential. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview about recent progress in the atomistic simulation of electrified interfaces using MLPs. Current developments fall into three different categories. The first comprises linear response models that describe polarisation, polarisability, and Born effective charges, extending conventional MLPs to finite electric fields. The second includes methods that directly learn a field-dependent potential energy surface. The third consists of a series of hybrid approaches combining classical models with machine learning. Although still under active development, these methods represent a major step toward more realistic simulations approaching the quality of electronic structure calculations. Finally, we discuss open challenges and possible future directions for advancing MLP-based simulations aiming for a bottom-up understanding of atomistic processes at electrified interfaces.

title: AI4Plasma I: Data-Efficient Surrogate Modeling of Capacitively Coupled Plasma Fields
title_zh: 文献研究：AI4Plasma I: Data-Efficient Surrogate Modeling of Capacitively Coupled Plasma Fields
summary: Reference capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) simulations provide spatially resolved plasma fields but are costly to generate across operating conditions. We compare the data efficiency of five surrogat…
abstract: arXiv:2611.15002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reference capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) simulations provide spatially resolved plasma fields but are costly to generate across operating conditions. We compare the data efficiency of five surrogate architectures--Coordinate MLP, PCA-Net, U-Net, Fourier neural operator (FNO), and Transolver--for predicting RF-cycle-averaged electron density, ion density, electric potential, and electron temperature in 1D planar and 2D axisymmetric GEC CCP benchmarks. We assess the number of reference simulations needed to achieve 1% and 2% mean relative L2 error for parameter-interior and parameter-boundary test cases, and examine architecture-specific mechanisms. FNO achieves the lowest or joint-lowest reference-case requirement in seven of eight comparisons. In 1D, FNO reaches 1% interior error with 50 training cases, compared with 100 for Transolver and 200 for U-Net. In 2D, FNO and U-Net each reach 1% interior error with 100 cases; FNO and Transolver each reach 2% parameter-boundary error with 200 cases, compared with 400 for U-Net. At the stricter 1% 2D parameter-boundary target, Transolver requires 400 cases versus 800 for FNO. Additional analyses investigate FNO spectral modes and padding, U-Net skip connections, Transolver adaptive slicing, and PCA-Net projection versus prediction error. The results support FNO as a data-efficient baseline for the tested CCP settings, while showing that the preferred architecture depends on the accuracy target and operating-parameter region.

title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
title_zh: 文献研究：Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
summary: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to t…
abstract: arXiv:2611.16792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties. Our results show that the effectiveness of data acquisition strategies depend strongly on the interplay between the model, dataset, and prediction task, although uncertainty-based sampling generally outperforms alternative strategies. Based on these findings, we derive guidelines for selecting data acquisition strategies under a given labelling budget.

title: Partition of Unity Data-driven Finite Element Method for Anisotropic Diffusion in Magnetized Plasmas
title_zh: 文献研究：Partition of Unity Data-driven Finite Element Method for Anisotropic Diffusion in Magnetized Plasmas
summary: Numerical simulation of transport processes in magnetized plasmas is characterized by extreme anisotropy, where diffusion along magnetic field lines can be many orders of magnitude larger than in the…
abstract: arXiv:2611.17086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Numerical simulation of transport processes in magnetized plasmas is characterized by extreme anisotropy, where diffusion along magnetic field lines can be many orders of magnitude larger than in the perpendicular direction. This anisotropy leads to thin, steep boundary layers and numerical pollution that standard finite element methods struggle to resolve without prohibitive mesh refinement. In this paper, we introduce the Partition of Unity Data-Driven Finite Element Method (PU-DDFEM), a data-driven local model reduction approach, for anisotropic diffusion. The method utilizes a bottom-up construction to enable a complete offline-online splitting. We parametrize the local magnetic field and boundary conditions to generate a snapshot space that captures the essential physics of plasma confinement. Dominant modes are extracted via a local spectral problem to identify representative features. These modes are then mapped to the global domain using a partition of unity to form a conforming approximation space. This ensures that the basis functions are fully reusable across different global magnetic configurations, significantly reducing the online computational overhead for large-scale plasma simulations.

title: HARMONY: an efficient and accurate deep learning framework for prediction of experimental vibrational spectra
title_zh: 文献研究：HARMONY: an efficient and accurate deep learning framework for prediction of experimental vibrational spectra
summary: Predicting experimental vibrational spectra requires both efficient molecular calculations and a reliable mapping from theoretical vibrations to measured signals. Here we introduce HARMONY, a two-stag…
abstract: arXiv:2611.16342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting experimental vibrational spectra requires both efficient molecular calculations and a reliable mapping from theoretical vibrations to measured signals. Here we introduce HARMONY, a two-stage deep-learning framework that bridges this gap using harmonic spectra as physical anchors. Equivariant neural networks directly predict atomic forces and spectroscopic tensors for rapid harmonic-spectrum construction, while HarmoNet combines these spectra with molecular topology and measurement metadata to predict experimental infrared and Raman spectra. HARMONY achieves mean cosine similarities of 0.912 for infrared and 0.907 for Raman spectra, with a mean inference time of 2.12~s per molecule, approximately 600-fold faster than the evaluated DFT workflow. Beyond forward prediction, HARMONY improves inverse molecular inference through pseudo-experimental pretraining and spectral verification of candidate structures. Integrating HARMONY and Vib2Mol as scientific tools within a general-purpose agent enables adaptive candidate generation and verification. With molecular formulas provided, the resulting Vib2Mol--HARMONY Agent achieves Top-1 recall of 70.53% on NIST using infrared spectra and 83.33% on SDBS using combined infrared and Raman spectra. Fine-tuning with 19 amino-acid controls and eight peptides further increases mean Raman cosine similarity from 0.669 to 0.896 on 15 held-out peptides. HARMONY establishes harmonic anchoring as a practical connection between molecular physics, experimental spectroscopy and adaptive molecular structure elucidation.

title: Are Scaling Laws of Universal MLIPs Universal?
title_zh: 文献研究：Are Scaling Laws of Universal MLIPs Universal?
summary: Neural scaling laws enable the prediction of returns from larger training datasets, but machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) datasets are heterogeneous and expensive to generate, and equal num…
abstract: arXiv:2611.15603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural scaling laws enable the prediction of returns from larger training datasets, but machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) datasets are heterogeneous and expensive to generate, and equal numbers of structures need not contain equal amounts of useful information. We study data scaling under fixed model configurations for M3GNet, MACE, and PET trained on subsets of a combined MatPES-MP-ALOE training pool. Across training structure subsets from 10,000 to 640,000, together with the full 1.16-million-structure training set, we compare uniform random sampling, three chemistry- and structure-informed stratification policies, iterative DIRECT, and furthest-point sampling using embeddings from three pretrained MLIPs. Models are evaluated using cohesive-energy, force, stress, and aggregate losses on both a held-out test set from the parent distribution and the distribution shifted MP-r²SCAN test set. We observe power-law scaling improvements with increasing data, but the fitted scaling exponent, apparent error floor, and relative sample efficiency depend on the model architecture, target quantity, data sampling policy, and test set distribution. Sampling-policy rankings can reverse across test distributions: chemical stratification can improve cross-dataset performance while degrading in-distribution performance, whereas the embedding-space diversity policies frequently under-perform random sampling. Relative loss is strongly associated with test-to-train chemical-space divergence. These results show that structure count is a necessary but insufficient scaling variable for MLIPs. For training MLIPs, the return on additional first-principles calculations depends not only on how many additional structures are included, but also on how their chemical and configurational content aligns with the model's intended use.

title: Materials research with a general-purpose agent
title_zh: 使用通用代理进行材料研究
summary: 在过去十年中，我们建立了 Alexandria，这是一个包含约 1500 万个晶体密度泛函计算的开放数据库。它包括 PBE、PBEsol、SCAN 和 TB-mBJ 结果、在高达 150 GPa 的压力下松弛的结构、介电张量和约 145,000 个电子声子计算，以及超过 4 亿个通过机器学习势松弛的结构。根据这些数据，我们训练了晶体结构的生成模型、通用原子间势以及从带隙到超导临界温度等十多种属性的图神经网络。
abstract: arXiv:2611.15451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over the last decade we have built Alexandria, an open database of about 15 million density-functional calculations of crystals. It includes PBE, PBEsol, SCAN and TB-mBJ results, structures relaxed at pressures up to 150 GPa, dielectric tensors and about 145,000 electron-phonon calculations, together with more than 400 million structures relaxed with machine-learned potentials. On these data we trained a generative model for crystal structures, a universal interatomic potential and graph neural networks for more than ten properties, from band gaps to superconducting critical temperatures. From the convex hull we computed a reaction graph of the 17.4 billion reactions between its 193,416 stable compounds. Here we give all of this to a general-purpose language-model agent. Working unattended, the agent screens the database for a solar absorber, drops a candidate whose synthesis releases too little energy, and writes a synthesis plan with precursors, crucible and atmosphere. Asked about the well-studied Ba-Zr-S system, it finds an unreported sulfide and designs the experiment that would confirm or rule it out. Asked for an air-stable alternative, it designs one and tests it against new structures from the generative model. With web search alone, the same agent proposes what the literature already discusses. Put together, the data, the models and the reaction graph let a general agent do what none of them does alone: go from a question in plain words to an experiment that a laboratory can run and test.

title: Coupled Electronic Structure and Phonon Transport Driven by Bonding Reconstruction in Ba-B-C Clathrates
title_zh: 文献研究：Coupled Electronic Structure and Phonon Transport Driven by Bonding Reconstruction in Ba-B-C Clathrates
summary: Composition-driven changes in electron count, structural symmetry and bonding environment can couple the electronic and thermal responses in a material. Here, with density-functional theory and machin…
abstract: arXiv:2609.32894v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Composition-driven changes in electron count, structural symmetry and bonding environment can couple the electronic and thermal responses in a material. Here, with density-functional theory and machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), we compare cubic BaB3C3 with its B-C substituted tetragonal counterpart, BaB2C4. The additional valence electron and accompanying change in crystal symmetry drive a transition from metallic BaB3C3 to semiconducting BaB2C4 and the formation of short/strong C-C bonds. The reconstructed bonding network hardens the phonon spectrum, with the maximum frequency increasing from 800 to 900. At room temperature, the in-plane lattice thermal conductivity increases from 7.6 to 18.7 W/mK, while the thermal transport alters from isotropic to anisotropic for BaB2C4. This enhancement is associated with the strengthened bonding network, higher phonon frequencies/group velocities, longer lifetimes and larger mean free paths. Machine learning potentials accurately reproduced the DFT-level energies and forces with negligible errors, and the harmonic and anharmonic features are benchmarked against explicit first-principles calculations. Our findings demonstrate that minimal B-C substitution provides a viable strategy to link composition- and structure-associated bonding reconstruction with correlated electronic and phononic alterations.

title: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
title_zh: 文献研究：From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
summary: Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behaviour of CaCO₃ in wate…
abstract: arXiv:2603.06800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behaviour of CaCO₃ in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO₃ with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the ''gold-standard'' coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO₃ ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.

title: Brute-force molecular dynamics simulation of aging in amorphous Ge₂Sb₂Te₅
title_zh: 非晶态 Ge2Sb2Te5 老化的强力分子动力学模拟
summary: 硫属化物合金，例如典型的 Ge2Sb2Te5 化合物，由于其在加热时能够在非晶相和晶相之间进行快速且可逆的转变，因此被用于相变电子存储器。非晶相容易老化，导致电阻增加，这不利于器件的运行。利用机器学习原子间势，我们在略低于玻璃化转变的温度下，在分子动力学模拟中研究了导致非晶态 Ge2Sb2Te5 老化的结构弛豫。时效模拟持续约 100 ns，在 400 K 下达到 24 ns 的平衡。
abstract: arXiv:2611.15664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chalcogenide alloys such as the prototypical Ge₂Sb₂Te₅ compound are used in phase change electronic memories due to their ability to undergo a fast and reversible transition between the amorphous and crystalline phases upon heating. The amorphous phase is subject to aging that leads to an increase in the electrical resistance, which is detrimental to the operation of the devices. Using a machine learning interatomic potential, we have investigated the structural relaxations responsible for aging in amorphous Ge₂Sb₂Te₅ in molecular dynamics simulations at temperatures slightly below the glass transition. The aging simulation, lasting about 100 ns, follows an equilibration of 24 ns at 400 K. During aging we observed an enhancement of the Peierls distortion in axial bonds which is a typical feature of these alloys that we relate to the widening of the electronic band gap computed within Density Functional Theory in smaller aged amorphous models. We also observed a marked reduction of the atomic mobility with an increase of the bond lifetimes during aging. However, we do not see a reduction in homopolar bonds, which are expected to be absent in the ideal aged glass and which should be removed on a much longer time scale.

title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and B-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃ Perovskite Alloys
title_zh: 竞争八面体倾斜和 B 位偏心控制 CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃ 钙钛矿合金的相图
summary: 基于Ge和Sn的无铅卤化物钙钛矿避免了Pb的毒性，但这两种阳离子有利于不同的结构扭曲。具有立体化学活性的 Ge 4s² 孤对电子驱动极性 B 位点偏心，而较大的 Sn²⁺ 阳离子则有利于八面体倾斜。在这里，我们使用大规模分子动力学模拟以及在混合功能数据上训练的电荷感知机器学习原子间势，绘制了这两种不稳定性如何在 CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃ 的整个组成范围内竞争。
abstract: arXiv:2611.15200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lead-free halide perovskites based on Ge and Sn avoid the toxicity of Pb, but the two cations favor different structural distortions. The stereochemically active Ge 4s² lone pair drives polar B-site off-centering, whereas the larger Sn²⁺ cation favors octahedral tilting. Here, we map how these two instabilities compete across the full composition range of CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃ using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential trained on hybrid-functional data. At low temperature the alloy exhibits a morphotropic phase boundary between x=0.60 and 0.65 that separates a ferroelectric monoclinic Cc phase from a monoclinic P2₁ phase with mixed antipolar and polar off-centering, with both the tilt pattern and the off-centering order changing discontinuously. The composition-temperature phase diagram reproduces the known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and reveals an intermediate tetragonal I4/mcm phase near the boundary that has no counterpart in either parent compound. Above the transition temperatures the B cations remain locally off-centered but orientationally disordered. The structural transition at the boundary causes a jump in the band gap at low temperature, whereas at 350 K the gap decreases smoothly with Sn content. These results establish B-site mixing as a means to tune polar and rotational order in lead-free halide perovskites.

title: Single Spin Hall Conversion in the Hall Response of Magnetic-Insulator/Heavy-Metal Bilayers Identified by Odd Spin-Hall-Angle Dependence
title_zh: 由奇自旋霍尔角依赖性识别的磁绝缘体/重金属双层霍尔响应中的单自旋霍尔转换
summary: 磁绝缘体/重金属双层的霍尔响应通常归因于两个连续的自旋霍尔转换，因此预计自旋霍尔角是均匀的。使用不同的磁场窗口，我们将具有相反自旋霍尔角的 Ta 和 Pt 的钇铁石榴石双层的霍尔电压分为磁化和磁场驱动的进动以及普通霍尔效应的贡献。场驱动组件反转 Ta 和 Pt 之间的符号，揭示霍尔响应奇数自旋霍尔角。除了最薄的重金属层外，磁化驱动成分对于 Ta 和 Pt 也具有相反的符号。
abstract: arXiv:2611.15571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hall response of magnetic-insulator/heavy-metal bilayers is usually ascribed to two successive spin Hall conversions and is therefore expected to be even in the spin Hall angle. Using distinct magnetic-field windows, we separate the Hall voltage of yttrium iron garnet bilayers with Ta and Pt of opposite spin Hall angle into contributions from magnetization- and magnetic-field-driven precession as well as from ordinary Hall effect. The field-driven component reverses sign between Ta and Pt, revealing a Hall response odd-in-spin-Hall-angle. The magnetization-driven component also has opposite signs for Ta and Pt, except for the thinnest heavy-metal layers. A drift-diffusion model with interface-generated spin currents describes this behavior: the field-driven component is predominantly carried by a single spin Hall conversion, and the magnetization-driven component is consistent with one as well. Other potential explanations, based on a description with a finite imaginary spin-mixing conductance rather than interface-generated spin currents, require unusually large values of this conductance, making this mechanism unlikely. Our findings advance the understanding of Hall responses in magnetic-insulator/heavy-metal bilayers toward a more general description.

title: Model Order Reduction for Quantum Molecular Dynamics
title_zh: 文献研究：Model Order Reduction for Quantum Molecular Dynamics
summary: Quantum molecular dynamics (QMD) provides a high-fidelity physical framework for modeling atomic and molecular phenomena from first principles. However, its mathematical formulation requires solving i…
abstract: arXiv:2509.07340v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum molecular dynamics (QMD) provides a high-fidelity physical framework for modeling atomic and molecular phenomena from first principles. However, its mathematical formulation requires solving iterative, high-dimensional electronic structure problems at every physical state step. Within the broader data-driven computational mechanics paradigm, we present a projection-based model order reduction framework for electronic structure calculation in QMD. By discovering a low-dimensional manifold of the electronic solution space within Kohn-Sham density functional theory, our approach projects the governing variational formulation onto an intrinsically reduced subspace. This avoids full-space iterative wavefunction optimization while preserving rigorous physical symmetries and state consistency. We demonstrate this methodology on a water molecule, demonstrating strong agreement with high-fidelity reference solutions across structural trajectories and thermodynamic observables through canonical coordinate alignment and structured manifold sampling.

title: High-Throughput Surface Screening Reveals Energetically Competitive Low-Symmetry Facets in Wurtzite Semiconductors
title_zh: 高通量表面筛选揭示了纤锌矿半导体中具有能量竞争力的低对称面
summary: 表面和界面决定着纤锌矿半导体在电子、传感和太阳能燃料转换方面的性能。迄今为止，由于低对称高折射率表面建模的计算成本和复杂性，第一原理研究主要集中在高对称低折射率面。然而，实际上，表面形成能是由平面原子密度和解理时切断的键的强度决定的，这两者都本质上排除了高米勒指数表面的能量竞争。在这里，我们结合自动表面生成、机器学习原子间势筛选和密度泛函理论，探索了纤锌矿 GaN、LaN 和 ZnO 的 226 个干净的化学计量表面模型，涵盖所有米勒方向 |h|、|k|、|l| 。
abstract: arXiv:2611.15138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surfaces and interfaces govern the performance of wurtzite semiconductors in electronics, sensing, and solar-fuel conversion. To date, first-principles studies have focused mostly on high-symmetry low-index facets, owing to the computational cost and complexity of modelling low-symmetry high-index surfaces. In practice, however, surface formation energy is determined by the planar atomic density and the strength of the bonds severed upon cleavage, neither of which inherently excludes high-Miller-index surfaces from being energetically competitive. Here, we combine automated surface generation, machine-learning interatomic potential screening, and density functional theory to explore 226 clean, stoichiometric surface models of wurtzite GaN, LaN, and ZnO, spanning all Miller orientations with |h|,|k|,|l| le 3 and their inequivalent terminations. We find that low-symmetry high-index prismatic facets are energetically competitive with respect to the conventional m- and a-planes: nine of the fifteen lowest-energy nonpolar surfaces are high-index, and the five best candidates of each compound lie within only 2.5-5.3% of the minimum surface energy. Hybrid-functional calculations reveal, however, that this energetic proximity does not translate into similar electronic alignment. In GaN, the two most stable surfaces differ by just 0.08 J m⁻² in formation energy but by almost 0.8 eV in vacuum-referenced band-edge positions, whereas in LaN the nearly degenerate m- and a-planes are separated by 0.16 eV. Wurtzite facets with similar formation energies may therefore exhibit very different ionization potentials and electron affinities. Our results enable the joint, systematic assessment of stability and band alignment across the facets that can actually occur in wurtzites, and provide a map of candidate surfaces for the rational design of related nanostructure and heterointerfaces.

title: A System-Independent Metadynamics Strategy for Reactive Training Data: Application to Gas-Phase Organic Reactions
title_zh: 文献研究：A System-Independent Metadynamics Strategy for Reactive Training Data: Application to Gas-Phase Organic Reactions
summary: General-purpose machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for organic reactions need to accurately describe both minimum-energy paths (MEPs) for evaluating reaction energetics and the broader co…
abstract: arXiv:2609.29105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: General-purpose machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for organic reactions need to accurately describe both minimum-energy paths (MEPs) for evaluating reaction energetics and the broader configurational space for simulating reaction dynamics. Existing general datasets for gas-phase reactions largely rely on quasi-static optimization near MEPs, leaving off-MEP regions under-covered and model reliability in reactive molecular dynamics weakly supported; the gap is methodological, not a question of dataset size. We introduce a spatiotemporally resolved, system-independent collective variable (CV): Cartesian RMSD within randomly partitioned local domains against an expanding list of time-averaged reference geometries. The CV drives metadynamics as the exploration engine, supplemented by transition state (TS) optimization to augment coverage around TSs. Within a concurrent-learning workflow, this produces OpenRxn26, a dataset of 1.8~M DFT-labeled configurations covering neutral singlet unimolecular reactions in the H/C/N/O chemical space (N_heavy ≤ 30), containing reactive atomic environments underrepresented in community datasets. Trained on OpenRxn26, a DPA4 model (DPA4_rxn26) is the only model in the benchmark suite to achieve transferable sub-kcal/mol energy accuracy on barrier heights, reaction energies and off-MEP reactive trajectories, relative to the training DFT reference, demonstrating the efficiency and generality of the sampling strategy. Domain MLIPs performing well on static benchmarks degrade several-fold on off-MEP reactive trajectories (e.g. MACE-OMol25), showing the insufficiency of MEP-anchored benchmarks for guaranteeing dynamics reliability. The sampling strategy enables efficient development of reliable general-purpose reactive MLIPs, with OpenRxn26 as a demonstration of MD-ready training data for gas-phase neutral singlet organic reactions.

title: Machine-accelerated extraction of experimental superconducting parameters for physical insight and prediction across thousands of materials
title_zh: 机器加速提取实验超导参数，以实现对数千种材料的物理洞察和预测
summary: 新的超导体可以解锁从核聚变到无损电子学的下一代技术。机器学习可以预测候选超导体，但缺乏超过临界温度的经过验证的实验训练数据。在这里，我们介绍 AutoSuperCon，一个包含 8 个超导参数的数据库，其中包含 6793 个超导体的 20354 个条目。使用大型语言模型从 47000 多个 arXiv 预印本中提取数据，并根据参考数据集进行验证（NIMS SuperCon 的 R² = 0.96）。
abstract: arXiv:2611.15627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: New superconductors could unlock next-generation technologies from nuclear fusion to lossless electronics. Machine learning can predict candidate superconductors but lacks validated experimental training data beyond the critical temperature. Here we present AutoSuperCon, a database of eight superconducting parameters, containing 20354 entries for 6793 superconductors. The data were extracted from over 47000 arXiv preprints using a large language model and validated against reference datasets (R² = 0.96 with NIMS SuperCon). Using AutoSuperCon, we show that median gap ratios rise from 3.6 in conventional superconductors to 6.4 in cuprates, 28% of upper critical fields exceed the Pauli limit, and critical temperatures lie below a ceiling proportional to the superfluid density. Further, we train composition-based predictors for the critical temperature (R²ₗₒg=0.83) and the upper critical field (R²ₗₒg=0.69), boosted by transfer learning. Within known superconducting families, composition alone is sufficient to screen candidates for both parameters. AutoSuperCon thus enables physical insight and data-driven discovery across thousands of superconductors.

title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
title_zh: 文献研究：Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
summary: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials,…
abstract: arXiv:2611.16016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

title: Local B-site chemistry controls oxygen-vacancy energetics in Ca-Ce-Ti-Mn perovskites for thermochemical hydrogen production
title_zh: 文献研究：Local B-site chemistry controls oxygen-vacancy energetics in Ca-Ce-Ti-Mn perovskites for thermochemical hydrogen production
summary: Two-step thermochemical water splitting driven by concentrated solar heat is a scalable route to renewable hydrogen, but it requires oxides whose oxygen-vacancy formation energies balance facile reduc…
abstract: arXiv:2607.28752v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-step thermochemical water splitting driven by concentrated solar heat is a scalable route to renewable hydrogen, but it requires oxides whose oxygen-vacancy formation energies balance facile reduction with favorable reoxidation. Perovskite solid solutions can tune this balance, but the relationship between bulk stoichiometry and local defect energetics remains poorly understood. Here we map oxygen-vacancy formation energetics across Ca-Ce-Ti-Mn (CCTM) perovskites by combining first-principles calculations with a coverage-constrained special quasirandom structure approach that realizes all fifteen symmetry-distinct oxygen nearest-neighbor environments, an interpretable crystal-feature model whose fitted coefficients directly encode the underlying Born-Haber thermochemistry, and a fine-tuned defect graph neural network. Local B-site chemistry dominates the oxygen-vacancy formation energy Eᵥ: varying the nearest-neighbor Mn fraction shifts Eᵥ by 1.0-1.5 eV depending on local Ce content, whereas A-site Ce variation contributes a smaller, Mn-dependent shift of 0.2-0.6 eV. Short-range B-site cation order, if it can be established and kinetically retained through processing, is therefore a candidate means of tuning redox performance without changing bulk composition. Composition-space maps identify a Ce/Mn-balanced region (~29-33% Ce on the A site and 58-67% Mn on the B site) combining a high fraction of vacancy sites within the targeted Eᵥ window with phase stability and solubility, whose predicted redox cycle capacity matches or exceeds the ceria benchmark at 1350 ^circC rather than the roughly 1600 ^circC ceria requires. Measurements on three CCTM compositions show cycle capacity increasing monotonically with Ce content under protocols close to the model conditions. The design rules are expected to transfer to related perovskite families.

title: SHRX: a neural surrogate of turbulent transport in tokamak plasma and its comparison with TORAX against experimental data
title_zh: 文献研究：SHRX: a neural surrogate of turbulent transport in tokamak plasma and its comparison with TORAX against experimental data
summary: Integrated tokamak modelling needs fast surrogates of turbulent transport, but existing ones depend on JAX. We built SHRX, a neural network with 29,283 parameters that runs on NumPy alone, by distilli…
abstract: Integrated tokamak modelling needs fast surrogates of turbulent transport, but existing ones depend on JAX. We built SHRX, a neural network with 29,283 parameters that runs on NumPy alone, by distilling the QuaLiKiz neural network (QLKNN). A “bridge” converts the state of our one-and-a-half-dimensional simulator SINTEZ into the ten dimensionless QLKNN inputs. For stiff transport we introduce the error of the critical-gradient factor, (:δ:f), as a metric, and an ensemble of five networks gives an uncertainty estimate. We compare SINTEZ with SHRX against the TORAX code at three levels: identical local plasma states, an integrated ITER discharge with identical inputs, and 206 conventional and 41 spherical records of the H-mode database of the International Tokamak Physics Activity (ITPA). On machines held out of training, the median error of the heat diffusivity (:χ:) is 9% and the median (:δ:f) is 2.3%; the ensemble lowers the (:χ:) error to 5.9–6.5%. The ITER fusion power is 492 MW with SINTEZ and SHRX, 478 MW with SINTEZ and QLKNN, and 532 MW with TORAX. On experimental records the two codes agree with each other ((:r=0.995) in (:lnW)) better than with the measurements, and both are less accurate than the IPB98(y,2) regression ((:σ:ₗₙ) of 0.55 and 0.56 against 0.21). On spherical tokamaks SHRX overestimates the stored energy by a median factor of 28. SHRX is a faster, JAX-free copy of QLKNN, not a better model than TORAX: most of the experimental error comes from inputs that both codes share.

title: Nested Ensemble Learning with Topological Data Analysis for Graph Classification and Regression
title_zh: 文献研究：Nested Ensemble Learning with Topological Data Analysis for Graph Classification and Regression
summary: We propose a nested ensemble learning framework that utilizes Topological Data Analysis (TDA) to extract and integrate topological features from graph data, with the goal of improving performance on c…
abstract: arXiv:2611.14900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a nested ensemble learning framework that utilizes Topological Data Analysis (TDA) to extract and integrate topological features from graph data, with the goal of improving performance on classification and regression tasks. Our approach computes persistence diagrams (PDs) using lower-star filtrations induced by three filter functions: closeness, betweenness, and degree2 centrality. To overcome the limitation of relying on a single filter, these PDs are integrated through a data-driven, three-level architecture. At Level-0, diverse base models are independently trained on the topological features extracted for each filter function. At Level-1, a meta-learner combines the predictions of these base models for each filter to form filter-specific ensembles. Finally, at Level-2, a meta-learner integrates the outputs of these filter-specific ensembles to produce the final prediction. We evaluate our method on both simulated and real-world graph datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms base models and standard stacking methods, achieving higher classification accuracy and lower regression error. It also surpasses existing state-of-the-art approaches, ranking among the top three models across all benchmarks.
